:::{#thm-matrix-inner-product-entries}
#### The matrix inner product multiplies matching entries

For two $n \times p$ matrices $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$:

$$
\iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}} = \sumin \sumjp a_{ij}\, b_{ij}
$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}
&= \tr(\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{B})
&& \text{(definition of the inner product)}
\\
&= \sumjp (\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{B})_{jj}
&& \text{(definition of the trace)}
\\
&= \sumjp \sumin (\tp{\matr{A}})_{ji}\, b_{ij}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \sumjp \sumin a_{ij}\, b_{ij}
&& \text{(definition of the transpose)}
\\
&= \sumin \sumjp a_{ij}\, b_{ij}
&& \text{(swap the order of two finite sums)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-matrix-inner-product}
#### The inner product of two $2 \times 2$ matrices

Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
$$

From @def-matrix-inner-product:

$$
\ba
\iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}
&= \tr\paren{\tp{\matr{A}}\matr{B}}
&& \text{(definition of the inner product)}
\\
&= \tr\paren{
\tp{\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}}
\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
}
&& \text{(substitute)}
\\
&= \tr\paren{
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
}
&& \text{(definition of the transpose)}
\\
&= \tr\paren{\begin{bmatrix} -3 & 7 \\ -4 & 10 \end{bmatrix}}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -3 + 10
&& \text{(definition of the trace)}
\\
&= 7
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

From @thm-matrix-inner-product-entries:

$$
\ba
\iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}
&= 1 \cd 0 + 2 \cd 1 + 3 \cd (-1) + 4 \cd 2
&& \text{(multiply matching entries and add)}
\\
&= 0 + 2 - 3 + 8
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= 7
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-matrix-inner-product-dot-product}
#### The matrix inner product as a dot product

@thm-matrix-inner-product-entries says that the matrix inner product
is the dot product (@def-dot-product) of the two matrices'
entries, each listed as one vector of length $np$,
with both matrices' entries listed in the same order.

For example, listing the entries of $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$
in @exm-matrix-inner-product row by row
gives $(1, 2, 3, 4)$ and $(0, 1, -1, 2)$,
and $(1, 2, 3, 4) \cdot (0, 1, -1, 2) = 7 = \iprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}$.

:::
